subject: Re: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC discovery & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC discovery & next steps

Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Regulatory mandate requiring all PHI/NPI to remain in your VPC (data residency + isolation).
- Network restrictions: no outbound internet egress from the air-gapped processing cluster; strict firewall whitelists managed by your networking team.
- KMS/HSM requirement: customer-managed key material for any persistent storage of embeddings/logs.
- Procurement timeline: security review + procurement expected in ~6–8 weeks; pilot desired before EOY.

Goals we discussed:
- Run a Private (VPC) deployment inside AcmeHealth-controlled subnets with optional air-gap for inference workloads.
- Ensure no egress of raw data; only allow approved telemetry (minimal usage metrics) to Redwoods' control plane if acceptable, else control-plane-less (on-prem) option.
- Deliver a 2-week pilot supporting a single LLM route (clinical summarization) with SLA-like latency targets and cost guidance.

Technical summary / constraints:
- Networking: You will require either VPC peering + restricted NAT for outbound to our image registry and metrics endpoints, or an air-gapped on-prem appliance image we can ship and customers install.
- Data at rest: Customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own keys) for embeddings and logs.
- Audit: SOC2 reports + architecture diagram will be provided; legal wants an inventory of endpoints that the control plane hits.

Next steps (owners + ETA):
1) I will circulate the high-level Private/VPC tech brief and the template network requirements (attached). Action: Marissa — EOD Mon (2026-07-13).
2) Tom to confirm whether AcmeHealth networking team prefers VPC peering with NAT vs fully air-gapped appliance and share contact info for network lead (Priya). Action: Tom/Priya — by Wed (2026-07-15).
3) Rishi to prepare a short pre-pilot checklist (hosted components, expected ports, cert/KMS notes) and a candidate pilot plan. Action: Rishi — Thu (2026-07-16).
4) Align on procurement path and legal questions (Priya/Acme legal). Action: Tom/Priya — ongoing.

Attachments: acmehealth_network_requirements.xlsx (network ports, CIDR examples), redwood_private_vpc_template.pdf (deployment options and roles).

Links: HubSpot deal and shared Drive folder included below.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the succinct recap, this aligns with what I have. A few clarifications / notes from our side:

- Network lead: Priya is on copy; she will be the primary for firewall/NAT conversations.
- Preferred deployment: our security team prefers an air-gapped pattern where possible; however, for an initial pilot we may accept tightly controlled egress to a hardened registry and metrics endpoint. We need to confirm the exact FQDNs and IP ranges.
- KMS: We can provide customer-managed keys via our KMS (on AWS GovCloud for some workloads). Need guidance on key rotation and HSM compatibility.
- Timeline: procurement is painful but target pilot kickoff in late August if approvals move. We will push for the 6–8 week window you called out.

Action items from my side:
- Priya to share a short network contacts list and initial list of blocked ports.
- I will review the attached network requirements this week and flag any immediate redlines.

Also: our legal team will likely ask for a list of third-party endpoints your control plane hits and an example SLA/addendum. If you can provide a one-pager for procurement/legal that would speed approvals.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
AcmeHealth
